account: In January 2025 Metropolitan Police Live Facial Recognition (LFR) cameras on a van at Denmark Hill identified David Cheneler, 73. He was under a 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order barring him from being alone with children under 14. The order followed a 2010 conviction for 15 counts of indecent assault on a female under 16 and five of gross indecency with a child. Officers found him with a six-year-old girl he had collected from school for her mother. The mother did not know his history. A lock knife was hidden in his belt buckle. He pleaded guilty at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on 13 January 2025 to breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon. On 20 May 2025 Kingston Crown Court jailed him for two years.

ai_role.statement: The LFR system did the identification. Cameras on the back of a van at Denmark Hill matched Cheneler's face and alerted officers, Southwark News reports. Finding the child and the knife, the arrest, the charges and the sentence were human and judicial acts. The offense itself existed only because of his 2019 order. The counterfactual is the Met's own hedge. DC Adam Pearce said it is possible that, had he not been identified, Cheneler could have gone on to abuse the child. No allegation about this occasion is reported. The readable source does not name the vendor or algorithm. The Met's press release is not among the sources.

fields.account: In January 2025 Metropolitan Police Live Facial Recognition (LFR) cameras on a van at Denmark Hill identified David Cheneler, 73. He was under a 2019 Sexual Offences Prevention Order barring him from being alone with children under 14. The order followed a 2010 conviction for 15 counts of indecent assault on a female under 16 and five of gross indecency with a child. Officers found him with a six-year-old girl he had collected from school for her mother. The mother did not know his history. A lock knife was hidden in his belt buckle. He pleaded guilty at Wimbledon Magistrates' Court on 13 January 2025 to breaching the order and possessing an offensive weapon. On 20 May 2025 Kingston Crown Court jailed him for two years.
